name: MonarchGoalTree
title: GoalTree
wrapsNative: Nested VStack rows with a Button toggle per goal (chevron, Expand/Collapse labels); ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear); MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchAvatar, MonarchFlowLayout, MonarchEmptyState
summary: Nested goals (objectives and key results) with progress, status, owner and alignment; branches open and close and each goal can carry its own actions.
whenToUse: For OKRs and other goal hierarchies, where readers scan progress and status and drill into the key results of an objective.
whenNotToUse: For a file or folder hierarchy without progress, use List(_:children:) or OutlineGroup (tree-view). For a flat list of tasks, use a List with MonarchOnboardingChecklist or rows.
api: MonarchGoalTree.init(_ goals: [MonarchGoal], expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isQuietChildren: Bool = true, labels: MonarchGoalTreeLabels = MonarchGoalTreeLabels(), canAddChild: ((MonarchGoal, Int) -> Bool)? = nil, onAddChild: (@MainActor (MonarchGoal) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: @escaping (MonarchGoal) -> Actions)

MonarchGoalTree.init(_ goals: [MonarchGoal], expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isQuietChildren: Bool = true, labels: MonarchGoalTreeLabels = MonarchGoalTreeLabels(), canAddChild: ((MonarchGoal, Int) -> Bool)? = nil, onAddChild: (@MainActor (MonarchGoal) -> Void)? = nil) where Actions == EmptyView

MonarchGoal.init(id: String, parentID: String? = nil, title: String, progress: Double, status: MonarchGoalStatus, ownerName: String? = nil, ownerAvatarURL: URL? = nil, meta: String? = nil, alignedTo: String? = nil)
enum MonarchGoalStatus { case notStarted, onTrack, atRisk, offTrack, done }

MonarchGoalTreeLabels.init(status: (@Sendable (MonarchGoalStatus) -> String)? = nil, expand: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, collapse: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, alignedTo: String? = nil, addChild: String? = nil, addChildTo: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, childCount: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, empty: String? = nil)

options.name: goals
options.description: Every goal, flat. Nesting comes from parentID; a missing or self-referencing parent makes a top-level goal, and a cycle stops at the first repeat.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The ids of open goals. Kept inside when nil, with every goal that has children open at first.

options.name: isQuietChildren
options.description: Children that are on track or not started hide their badge; their status is still spoken.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the status names, the button names, Aligned to, Add key result, the child count and the empty text.

options.name: canAddChild
options.description: Which goals get the add-child button, from the goal and its depth (0 at the top). Top-level goals when nil.

options.name: onAddChild
options.description: Adds an "Add key result" button inside the open goals canAddChild allows. Receives the parent; the app adds the goal.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of each goal's row, such as a Menu with Check in and History.

states.name: open
states.description: The chevron points down and the children (and the add button) are shown, indented.

states.name: closed
states.description: The chevron points toward the reading direction and the heading shows the number of children, such as "3 key results".

states.name: quiet children
states.description: Children on track or not started have no badge.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty state, No goals yet.

appearance: Top-level titles use the strong body role and children the body role. Status badges are subtle MonarchStatusBadge capsules in the neutral, info, warning, danger or success tone with a symbol. The bar uses the Monarch linear progress style (accent fill on the muted track) with the percentage in muted caption text. The same roles adapt to dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named OutlineGroup; it cannot be controlled from outside, cannot name its disclosure button "Expand …" and cannot show a child count or an add button, so the tree draws its own rows with a Button toggle. The progress bar is always in the accent colour because MonarchProgressViewStyle has no tone; the web colours the bar by status. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1 (the web takes 0 to 100). Titles, facts and alignment are plain strings. Android uses the same name and API shape. Several closures are optional (canAddChild, onAddChild). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canAddChild.
accessibility: Each goal is one element read as its title, status, owner, facts, alignment and, when closed, its number of children.
The goal's value is its progress as a percentage in the user's locale.
The open and close button is a separate element named "Expand …" or "Collapse …" with a 44-point target.
The add button is named "Add key result to …".
Status badges carry a symbol and a word, so status does not rely on colour; quiet children still speak their status.
The chevron's turn follows Reduce Motion; avatars are hidden from VoiceOver because the owner is in the goal's label.
edgeCases: Progress outside 0 to 1 is clamped; not-a-number and infinity read as 0%.
Long titles wrap; badges and facts flow onto the next line.
A goal whose only child is the add button still has a toggle.
Deep trees indent by half a touch target per level; keep them to three levels on a phone.
